requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs on node1 as a managed (systemd) service
requirements.summary: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service created with ExecStart, Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started; systemctl reports active, MainPID present, and /health and /inventory return valid JSON.

requirements.requirement: A memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory
requirements.summary: An unprotected memhog.py process (oom_score_adj=0) was launched and allowed to allocate memory until swap and RAM were nearly exhausted (used memory 1.9Gi/1.9Gi, swap used 1.2Gi at peak); dmesg subsequently recorded a genuine kernel OOM-killer invocation.

requirements.requirement: The kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
requirements.summary: dmesg directly shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1644 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0', matching the hog's PID and score; inventory-api's PID (1596, score -1000) is distinct and unaffected.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout and after the OOM event, without restart
requirements.summary: Post-OOM systemctl show reports NRestarts=0 and unchanged MainPID=1596 matching the pre-OOM baseline; /health and /inventory both returned valid, incrementing-request-count JSON responses before, during, and after the OOM event.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id 6aa805ba..., service active/enabled, working /health) was captured; a native systemctl reboot was issued with ack returned before disconnect; polling showed connection timeouts while down, then a changed boot_id (65a20cb6-af63...) confirming an actual restart; post-restart state shows the service active/enabled, auto-started, retaining OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, with NRestarts=0 and working endpoints. The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the same boot_id transition (before_prepare vs after_executor).

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, then directly demonstrated the required behavior: an unprotected memory-hog process drove the system into a genuine kernel OOM event (confirmed via dmesg), the kernel killed the hog (oom_score_adj=0) rather than inventory-api (oom_score_adj=-1000), and inventory-api continued serving /health and /inventory with zero restarts throughout. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for node1, with a directly observed pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of the service, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, bounded evidence.
limitations: The evidence bundle relies on executor-selected command excerpts rather than full raw logs; underlying command outputs were trusted as presented.
Temp files /tmp/oom_test_start_epoch and /tmp/reboot.log were left on node1 after the run per the after-executor snapshot diff, a very minor hygiene gap not otherwise corroborated beyond the diff.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands trace clearly to task goals: service deployment, the required OOM demonstration (bounded, later cleaned up), and the mandated restart protocol. Hog artifacts (/root/memhog.py, .pid, .log) were explicitly removed after the test (cmd-4827e9a64d4c4c7c). No failed or conflicting services, no unsafe exposure beyond the intended service port 8080, and package health remained consistent (manager=dnf) before and after. Minor residue: two small temp files (/tmp/oom_test_start_epoch, /tmp/reboot.log) created during the test/reboot process were left behind per the after-executor snapshot diff, though these are harmless bookkeeping artifacts rather than functional residue.
